title: Derived descent and K-flat normalization of the ordinary point sections-tensor comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\Ql$ in $\Qlb$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use sheaf-module derived categories $D(R_F)$ and module derived categories $D(\mathcal O_F)$, obtained by localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Let $\theta$ be the termwise sections-tensor map specified in [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor], and let $-\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$ be K-flat derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Ordinary sheaf scalar extension, module scalar extension, and termwise sections over $s$ preserve all quasi-isomorphisms. The functor on $D(R_E)$ induced by termwise ordinary sheaf scalar extension is canonically naturally isomorphic to $-\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$, with comparison fixed by the derived counit on each representative. Under this comparison, $\theta$ induces natural isomorphisms
$$\theta^D_{L/E,K}:\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)$$
for every $K\in D(R_E)$, without constructibility, boundedness, or completeness hypotheses. On every K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], this is the class of the termwise balanced map $\Gamma(s,P)\otimes\mathcal O_L\to\Gamma(s,P\otimes R_L)$, through the sections and tensor quasi-isomorphisms induced by $P\to K$; it is independent of the resolution. If $A(C)=\Gamma(s,C)\otimes\mathcal O_L$ and $B(C)=\Gamma(s,C\otimes R_L)$ on complexes and $K\xleftarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{f}J$ is a roof with $q$ a quasi-isomorphism, the localized transformation is characterized by
$$B(f)B(q)^{-1}\theta_K=\theta_J A(f)A(q)^{-1}.$$
Thus its naturality includes every derived morphism, not only morphisms between chosen K-flat representatives.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change (K-flat model); explicit exact-functor and roof comparison extracted from old proof step 3 of lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension, supporting the final paragraph of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point

proof.text: Write $T(F)=F\otimes_{R_E}R_L$, $V(N)=N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, and $\Gamma_F=\Gamma(s,-)$ on $R_F$-modules. The global datum has $k$ algebraically closed [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] applies to both $R_E$ and $R_L$. The coefficient-section identifications and exactness of $T,V$ are supplied by [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor]. Thus all four functors $T,V,\Gamma_E,\Gamma_L$ are additive exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] their termwise functors preserve every quasi-isomorphism and induce functors $T_D,V_D,\Gamma_{E,D},\Gamma_{L,D}$ on the unbounded derived categories. Hereafter suppress the canonical factorization isomorphisms when writing a complex for its localized object. In particular $A=V\Gamma_E$ and $B=\Gamma_LT$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms and have localized lifts $A_D=V_D\Gamma_{E,D}$ and $B_D=\Gamma_{L,D}T_D$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; exact-functor factorization, specialized using the two stated point lemmas

proof.text: Let $Q_E,Q_L$ be the localizations for $R_E,R_L$ and let $\mathbb LT=-\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$ be [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Its left-derived counit is a natural transformation $\epsilon_C:\mathbb LT(Q_EC)\to Q_L(TC)$. More precisely, use the left-derived construction of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] for the class of K-flat complexes with flat terms: [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives a quasi-isomorphism from an object of this class to every complex, and clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] says that $Q_LT$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms between these objects. The termwise functor on the homotopy category is exact (it is the composite of the triangulated $T_D$ with its localization, by step 1). Consequently this construction applies and its counit is an isomorphism on every member $P$ of that class. This is the left-derived functor already denoted $\mathbb LT$, with its canonical counit. Pull the counit back along complexes to their homotopy category when considering cochain maps.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, proof; derived.tex Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, dual clause

proof.text:
For any complex $C$, choose $q:P\to C$ as in [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Naturality of the counit gives
$$\epsilon_C\circ\mathbb LT(Q_Eq)=Q_L(Tq)\circ\epsilon_P.$$
The left-derived functor sends the isomorphism $Q_Eq$ to an isomorphism, $Q_L(Tq)$ is invertible by step 1, and $\epsilon_P$ is invertible by step 2. Hence
$$\epsilon_C=Q_L(Tq)\circ\epsilon_P\circ\mathbb LT(Q_Eq)^{-1}$$
is invertible for every $C$. This deduction uses no K-flatness of $C$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; explicit naturality equation for its derived counit

proof.text: Use the factorization $T_DQ_E\cong Q_LT$ of step 1 to view $\epsilon$ as a natural transformation between $\mathbb LTQ_E$ and $T_DQ_E$. These are functors on complexes inverting quasi-isomorphisms. By parts (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], it descends uniquely to a natural transformation $c:\mathbb LT\to T_D$, with $c_{Q_EC}=\epsilon_C$ under the factorization. Step 3 makes $\epsilon$ a natural isomorphism; the same localization result lifts its inverse, so $c$ is a natural isomorphism. The required comparison $T_D\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb LT$ is $c^{-1}$. Its normalization is fixed on every representative by the counit, and uniqueness follows from the same fully faithful precomposition property.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; natural-transformation enhancement as stated in the cited node, Mathlib Localization.liftNatIso

proof.text:
The termwise balanced maps of [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor] form a natural chain isomorphism $\theta:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. After applying the target localization, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] lifts it to a natural isomorphism $\tau:A_D\xrightarrow{\sim}B_D$ with component $[\theta_C]$ on each complex. Define
$$\theta^D_K=\Gamma_{L,D}(c_K^{-1})\circ\tau_K.$$
This has source $\Gamma_{E,D}(K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ and target $\Gamma_{L,D}(\mathbb LT K)$, exactly as required. Each factor is a natural isomorphism on all of $D(R_E)$; hence so is their composite.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; lift the existing balanced chain isomorphism, then compose with the counit-normalized comparison

proof.text:
For any K-flat resolution $q:P\to C$ with flat terms put
$$\rho_q=\epsilon_P\circ\mathbb LT(Q_Eq)^{-1}:\mathbb LT(Q_EC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_L(TP).$$
This is the canonical resolution comparison of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The equation of step 3 gives $c_{Q_EC}=Q_L(Tq)\rho_q$. Naturality of the balanced chain map gives $[B(q)]\,[\theta_P]=[\theta_C]\,[A(q)]$. Substitution into step 5 therefore gives
$$\theta^D_{Q_EC}=\Gamma_{L,D}(\rho_q^{-1})\circ[\theta_P]\circ[A(q)]^{-1}.$$
Here $A(q)=V(\Gamma_E(q))$ and $B(q)=\Gamma_L(Tq)$ are quasi-isomorphisms by step 1, so the inverses exist. Thus this is precisely the stated termwise balanced map through the sections and tensor quasi-isomorphisms. For any second resolution the identical calculation yields the same $\theta^D_{Q_EC}$; this proves independence without choosing a comparison cochain map between the resolutions.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; canonical K-flat computation and explicit substitution of the counit equation

proof.text:
For a roof $C\xleftarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{f}J$ with $q$ a quasi-isomorphism, chain naturality from [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor] reads
$$[B(f)][\theta_H]=[\theta_J][A(f)],\qquad [B(q)][\theta_H]=[\theta_C][A(q)].$$
Since $[A(q)]$ and $[B(q)]$ are invertible, the second equation gives $[B(q)]^{-1}[\theta_C]=[\theta_H][A(q)]^{-1}$. Multiplying by $[B(f)]$ and using the first equation yields
$$[B(f)][B(q)]^{-1}[\theta_C]=[\theta_J][A(f)][A(q)]^{-1}.$$
This is the requested formula (writing $K=C$ and suppressing brackets). It characterizes the localized transformation with the prescribed components by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. That result already supplies naturality for every derived morphism, and $c$ is natural as well, so the composite $\theta^D$ has that full naturality. All arguments used unbounded complexes and exact functors, with no constructibility or completeness assumption.
